body: Looks good. Thanks for the contribution.

The fix is needed, but I think the implementation should be simplified before merge.

Blocking correctness issue (simple-comment-editing.php:642)

WP_HTML_Processor::next_token() returns false both at normal EOF and when the processor encounters unsupported markup. This method always returns a successful parts array afterward and synthesizes the closing div, without checking get_last_error() or proving that the outer wrapper was closed. On WordPress 6.5 (the plugin minimum), the processor supports a limited element set. If another render_block_core/comment-content or render_block filter adds unsupported markup, this code can silently discard that token and everything after it. The advertised regex fallback is not reached for that failure mode.

Please avoid parsing and reserializing the complete rendered block. A simpler design would separate generation of the trusted SCE controls from wrapping the comment text: let Core render and sanitize core/comment-content, then attach the controls in the block render filter and give the JS an explicit comment-content target. That removes the three state properties, token serializer, and regex fallback while leaving Core responsible for its own markup. If the parser approach is retained, it must at least fail closed when get_last_error() is non-null or the outer closing tag was not observed, and it needs tests for unsupported and nested markup.

The regex fallback at simple-comment-editing.php:659 is also brittle because it relies on an exact wrapper shape and exact moderation-note attribute serialization. Since the plugin requires WordPress 6.5, WP_HTML_Processor already exists; this fallback mostly adds a second, less reliable parser rather than meaningful compatibility.

Evidence checked: WordPress Core render_block_core_comment_content() applies wp_kses() after comment_text; WordPress 6.5 has WP_HTML_Processor, but next_token() is documented as internal and its parser can stop on unsupported markup. PR CI currently only reports CodeRabbit and there are no repository tests covering these paths.
